title: One client-safe screen-wave contract: typed codes, guarded result, reason-aware 409s

body:
## Summary
The screen-wave has one server vocabulary and three hand-kept client copies of it. Put the wire contract (reason codes, decision/result types, the five refusal reasons and their runtime guards) in one import-free module that both sides import, and make the modal's state machine branch on the refusal reason the route already sends.

## Description
`runScreenWave` returns a closed `ScreenReasonCode` union and the route answers every approval refusal with a machine `reason`. The client never sees either. `decisionsScreenWaveTypes.ts` is a hand mirror that has drifted: `reasonCode` is a bare string, and `holdout: number` is declared required and pinned by a source-regex test even though the server never sends it. The two helpers written to render holdout keeps (`holdoutCount`, `waveKeepKind`) have no caller. The refusal guard sits in `screen-wave-approval.ts` behind `node:crypto`, so the client could not import it. As a result the modal folds all five 409s into a re-preview. An `unattributed` refusal loops (re-preview, commit, the same 409 again), and a `spent` refusal (the wave actually landed on a retried request) is reported as 'the set changed' while the queue behind the modal keeps showing people who were already rejected.

The move: `app/_lib/screen-wave-contract.ts` with no imports holds `SCREEN_REASON_CODES` (literal array, derived union), `ScreenDecision`, `ScreenWaveResult`, `SCREEN_WAVE_REFUSAL_REASONS` + `isScreenWaveRefusalReason`, `readWaveResult(payload)` and `readWaveRefusal(status, body)`. The server imports its types and re-exports them under the old names. The client types become aliases, and the phantom `holdout` field is deleted. The machine's `commitConflict` becomes `commitRefused{reason}` driven by a per-reason effect table, and the simulation walk reads the same guard.

## Flow
1. Create the contract module + its test (cases 1-4, 8) before touching callers.
2. Re-point screen-wave.ts / screen-wave-approval.ts to import from it and keep re-exports. tsc proves the server shape is unchanged.
3. Alias decisionsScreenWaveTypes.ts to the contract, drop `holdout`, and re-point decisionsFloorDisclosure.test.ts:80-87 to assert the alias instead of the phantom.
4. Replace commitConflict with commitRefused{reason} + REFUSAL_EFFECT table (repreview / blocked / landedElsewhere). Machine tests cover cases 5-7.
5. The hook folds the body through readWaveResult/readWaveRefusal, calls onCommitted() on landedElsewhere, and the modal disables Commit with the blocked reason in its existing aria-live line.
6. useSimulationWalk reads through readWaveResult, and the pipeline README section on the wave names the contract module.

## Expected impact
One authority per vocabulary: a new reason code or refusal becomes a type error in every consumer, where today it is a silent string. The open/keyless install's commit dead-end (no named approver) stops pretending a re-preview helps. A replayed commit that landed reloads the queue instead of leaving rejected candidates on screen with live buttons. The phantom field and its pinning test go away.

## Evaluation
Claim: the wave's wire contract has one client-safe source and the modal acts on the refusal reason the server sends.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (the contract module, commitRefused and landedElsewhere do not exist).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test cases in app/_lib/screen-wave-contract.test.ts and decisionsScreenWaveMachine.test.ts under npm run test:unit, plus tsc over the re-pointed imports.
Result: pending build.
Gate: none

title: Let the reviewer spare individuals from a wave, signed into the approval

Removal re-derives the token: the reviewer's exclusions are part of what they signed.' kp implements steps 1 and 3 but not the removal

screen-wave.ts:65-86 ScreenReasonCode is a closed union with per-code keep reasons (reinstated, holdout, ...); adding 'recruiterSpared' follows the existing shape, and pipelineEventCatalog.ts:117-120 / decision-attribution.ts:74-78 are where the sibling screen_wave_holdout event kinds are registered
rollback: The spare field is optional on the request and absent means byte-identical behaviour (empty effective spare adds no policyVersion suffix, so every existing token and sealed policyVersion is unchanged). Reverting the series removes the button, the field and the new reason code/event kind. Any `screen_wave_recruiter_spared` events already written are ordinary audit rows and remain readable.
runner_up: Show what moved on every re-preview: diff the new reject set against the last one the reviewer saw (entered / left the wave) so a 409 or slider drag is a targeted re-review, not a re-read of the whole list.
body:
## Summary
The screening wave is all-or-nothing. A recruiter who reads the preview and disagrees about one person has to drag a global slider, which reshapes everyone's outcome. Add a per-row 'Spare' in the preview. Spared people come back as keeps with the reason 'spared by you', the approval token is re-derived over the narrowed set, and the commit records who spared whom.

## Description
Today the Art. 22 review is a signature over a set the reviewer cannot edit. The registry's own procedure for this subject makes the reviewer's removals part of the signed set. The server already has the right shape for it: runScreenWave removes reinstated and holdout people from `wouldReject` before it signs the token, and the token is a hash of the sorted reject ids, so one more removal step before signing binds the recruiter's exclusions for free. The commit re-derives the same narrowed set from the echoed `spare` list, and a commit that drops the spares, or that carries a token minted without them, fails with the existing 'mismatch' 409.

New pieces: a pure `app/_lib/screen-wave-spare.ts` (normalizeSpareList: array of non-empty ids, de-duplicated, sorted, capped; effectiveSpare(wouldReject, spare) keeps only ids that would really be rejected); a `spare` option on runScreenWave and the route; a keep reason `recruiterSpared` with a localized line; a `screen_wave_recruiter_spared` human event on commit; and a `spared` set in the wave machine whose toggle forces a fresh preview. When the effective spare list is non-empty, policyVersion gets a `/spared<n>` suffix, so the sealed reject records say this wave had human exclusions. An empty list leaves the suffix off, which keeps policyVersion byte-identical to today's.

## Flow
1. Recruiter opens the wave. Each would-reject row gets a 'Spare' button beside its reason.
2. Clicking it moves the row to the kept list as 'Spared by you' with an Undo, triggers a debounced re-preview carrying `spare:[...]`, and returns a new token.
3. The commit echoes the same `spare` and token. The server re-derives the narrowed set, verifies the token and commits the rest. For each spared person it records the event and the approver.
4. The committed banner counts spared people separately from ordinary keeps.

## Expected impact
The reviewer can override one row, which is what makes the approval a review and not only a signature. Today one disagreement costs a slider move that rejects or spares other people nobody looked at, or it pushes the recruiter to commit and then use the reconsider queue after the rejection email has already gone out. Each exclusion is attributed and audited.

## Evaluation
Claim: a reviewer can remove individuals from a wave preview, the removal is bound into the approval token, and the commit honours exactly that narrowed set.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no spare field, reason code, event kind or machine state exists).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test in app/_lib/screen-wave-spare.test.ts, app/_lib/screen-wave.test.ts (temp-DB wave cases 2-5) and decisionsScreenWaveMachine.test.ts under npm run test:unit, plus npm run i18n:check for case 8.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract
